title: Delegated admin handover and shadow sync checklist for RBAC v2 migration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Owners: Security & Platform. This ticket captures a prescriptive checklist and runbook for transferring delegated administrator semantics from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 while ensuring audit log continuity and SSO/SAML mapping integrity. Focus areas: shadow-sync validation, dual-write safety net, canary waves for admin role handoff, explicit customer opt-out/consent flow, and automated verification that admin actions are attributed and auditable during and after cutover.
acceptance_criteria: Dual-write active with success rate >= 99.9% for 24h in canary orgs
Shadow sync reconciliation job detects and auto-corrects drift within 30 minutes for test dataset
All admin-facing APIs return identical semantics for delegated admin checks in RBAC v1 and v2 in canary region
Audit logs include an immutable mapping field 'auth_model_version' for every admin event during migration
Customer opt-out toggle functions and documented rollback flow verified with two pilot customers
migration_steps: Create canary cohort (20 orgs) with representative SSO and permission shapes
Enable dual-write on canary cohort; route writes to v1 authoritative store and v2 authoritative store in parallel
Run nightly shadow-sync reconciliation with verbose diff outputs to GCS
Deploy observability dashboard that tracks per-org dual-write success, shadow diff rate, and admin permission delta
Perform delegated admin handover in three waves: internal test orgs -> beta pilot customers -> broad canary cohort
Expose customer opt-out UI and API; verify access remains unchanged for opted-out customers
Once canary metrics stable for 72h, expand wave size and monitor closely before full cutover
rollback_plan: If dual-write success rate drops below 99% for >60 minutes, flip traffic to v1 authoritative store only
Re-run reconciliation and trigger on-call runbook to triage top-10 org diffs
Revoke RBAC v2 promo flags per-org via admin console and notify customer success
If audit gaps detected, freeze cutover and start forensic export of audit stream to S3 for replay
observability_checks: Shadow-sync diff rate (target < 0.1% of active principals)
KV cache warmup rate for admin calls post-handover
End-to-end latency for admin policy checks (<50ms p95)
Audit ingestion lag (<60s) and audit retention verification
audit_preservation_steps: Add 'auth_model_version' and 'handed_over_at' fields to every admin audit event during migration window
Stream audit logs to dedicated immutable S3/GCS bucket with ledger-style naming per-org
Enable per-org audit export job and verify schema backward compatibility with existing downstream analytics
Retention ensurement: run dry-run restore to a staging cluster quarterly
Add automated end-to-end tests that replay admin actions and assert audit artifacts exist and are verifiable
comms_plan: Pre-cutover: Doc published to /docs/rbac-v2/migration-summary with migration timeline and opt-out instructions
Pilot notice: email template for pilot customers with rollback SLA and expected dates
Cutover day: in-product banner for affected orgs with link to opt-out flow and support escalation
Post-cutover: summary report to customers highlighting audit continuity and any notable changes
Support playbook: triage matrix, customer-facing FAQ, and escalation contacts included in Confluence

notes: Trade-offs: We prefer dual-write + shadow sync to avoid surprises in permission checks, but this increases write-path complexity and requires strong observability. We chose to add an immutable audit field to simplify post-mortem attribution. Customers can opt-out during pilot; opt-outs will remain on RBAC v1 until customer consents to move. Key risk: SSO attribute mapping edge cases for nested external groups; mitigation: per-org reconciliation with human review for top-10 diffs.
